record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let a(n) be an integer sequence such that, for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b on X, the orbit b^{a(n)}Γ is equidistributed in X, and such that for every positive integer r the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Must a(n) then be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations, meaning that for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, there exists n with μ(A ∩ T1^{a(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{a(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Let (a(n)) be a sequence that satisfies: • for every connected `-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b in X the sequence (b^{a(n)}Γ)n∈N is equidistributed in X, and • the set {n ∈ N: r|a(n)} has positive upper density for every r ∈ N. Show that the sequence (a(n)) is good for `-recurrence of commuting transformations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integers satisfying both of the following conditions:

(i) For every positive integer $\ell$, every connected $\ell$-step nilmanifold $X = G/\Gamma$, and every irrational nilrotation $b \in G$ on $X$ (i.e., one for which the orbit $(b^n \Gamma)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is equidistributed in $X$), the sequence $(b^{a(n)} \Gamma)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is equidistributed in $X$.

(ii) For every positive integer $r$, the set $\{n \in \mathbb{N} : r \mid a(n)\}$ has positive upper density.

The sequence $(a(n))$ is said to be good for $\ell$-recurrence of commuting transformations if, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ equipped with $\ell$ commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$, and every measurable set $A\subseteq X$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$$\mu(A \cap T_1^{-a(n)}A \cap T_2^{-a(n)}A \cap \cdots \cap T_\ell^{-a(n)}A) > 0.$$

Prove or disprove: any sequence $(a(n))$ satisfying (i) and (ii) above is good for $\ell$-recurrence of commuting transformations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Frantzikinakis's open problem list on multiple ergodic averages. Recent work by Frantzikinakis–Kuca and others (e.g., on sparse corners, 2025) has obtained partial results for special sparse sequences like $[n^c]$ with non-integer $c$, advancing related conjectures, but no full resolution of the general implication has been published. The problem appears to remain open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys recent developments and provides a list of open problems regarding multiple recurrence and convergence phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic averages for sparse corners
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a framework for multiple ergodic averages with commuting transformations along sparse sequences, partially resolving several longstanding problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides partial results for special sparse sequences but not a full resolution.
